RagShortTexts: The standing military of Anteans in 374 AD relied upon veteran formations specialized in disciplined field deployment.
Combining heavy protective armor with specialized assault weaponry, the troops executed tactical doctrines honed in frontier engagements.
Commanders emphasized coordinated shock charges and defensive stability, preventing frontline collapse against aggressive cavalry raids.

Variants.Content: The martial renown of Anteans rested upon exhaustive drilling and veteran battlefield cohesion during the turbulent close of the 4th century. Core tactical doctrine integrated heavy shield formations with disciplined skirmishing wings, executing tactical maneuvers designed to absorb and counter enemy shock. Along vulnerable sectors, defensive engineers implemented field fortifications and obstacles, breaking the initial momentum of hostile assaults. Once enemy ranks faltered, armored shock reserves counter-charged under thunderous horn blasts, crushing exposed flanks with heavy swords and barbed spears. This balance of resilient endurance and ferocious striking power formed the military bedrock preserving Anteans against overwhelming regional adversaries.

Spearmen form a wall of shields in the muddy field, and the front line sets its feet to meet the horsemen. Each man counts his breath as the enemy approaches, and the sergeant walks the line to check that no one has stepped backward. When the first charge strikes the shields, the men holding the line can feel the ground shake beneath them.

Infantry will hold the river line while cavalry wheels around the flank through the forest, the council has decided. The supply convoy must cross the ford before the enemy can block the road. Send orders by a trusted messenger who knows the river paths, and do not share the flanking route with local chiefs, since their men may warn the enemy.
